title: Split text accessible name
prompt:
For each independent case provide diagnosis, smallest justified action, verification and limits. Do not claim execution. Treat each as a fresh product brief; cases do not authorize deployment or repository changes.

Hero headline is split into per-character `<span>` elements for a staggered entrance. To keep it readable, the developer put `aria-label="Build faster"` on the wrapping `<span class="split">` and left each character span exposed. Screen readers spell the headline letter by letter. Review and repair.

checks.reason: The answer must explain that aria-label on a generic span is prohibited or unreliable.
A visually hidden full-text copy is the correct accessible name source.
Keeping aria-label on a generic span is the anti-pattern.

rubric: The heading keeps one accessible text source (visually hidden copy or the original text) while the animated character spans are aria-hidden="true".
Reduced motion and a screen-reader check (reading the heading as one phrase) are part of verification.
Preserve the product intent and already-authorized scope. Do not claim actual browser, mutation, installation or deploy execution from a reasoning-only answer.
Give an observable check and a meaningful limit; keyword presence alone is not acceptance.
acceptance: The response makes the justified decision for this raw case, provides a discriminating verification and states the evidence limits without inventing execution.
